title: Minimum Wage Australia 18 Year Old: How to Convert Hourly Pay to Annual Salary
description: Learn how to calculate annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay from the minimum wage for an 18-year-old in Australia. Includes tax, super, and casual loading.
salarySummary: For an 18-year-old on the National Minimum Wage (adult rate $26.44/hour), assuming 38 hours per week, annual gross pay is about $52,245 before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the minimum wage for an 18-year-old in Australia?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage for adults is $26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026. For 18-year-olds, the Fair Work Commission sets a junior rate, typically 70% of the adult rate, which would be about $18.51 per hour. However, award rates may differ, and casual loading of 25% applies on top of the base rate.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52. For a full-time worker on 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, at the adult minimum wage of $26.44, annual gross is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,245.44.

faqs.q: Do I get superannuation on top of my minimum wage?
faqs.a: Yes. The super guarantee requires your employer to pay 12% of your ordinary earnings into a super fund, on top of your base wage. For an 18-year-old on the minimum wage, super is calculated on your gross pay (including casual loading if applicable) and is not deducted from your take-home pay.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Minimum Wage for an 18-Year-Old in Australia

If you're an 18-year-old worker in Australia, knowing your pay rate is the first step to managing your finances. The **minimum wage australia 18 year old** rate is not a single figure—it depends on whether you are covered by the National Minimum Wage or an award, and whether you work full-time, part-time, or casually. This guide explains how to convert your hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay, including tax and superannuation.

### The National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage each year. From 1 July 2026, the adult rate is **$26.44 per hour** for a 38-hour week, or **$1,004.90 per week**. However, for junior employees (under 21), the Commission applies a percentage of the adult rate. For an 18-year-old, the typical junior rate is **70%** of the adult minimum wage, which works out to about **$18.51 per hour**. This is the base rate before any casual loading.

Many 18-year-olds are covered by an award (industry or occupation-specific minimum pay). Awards often have higher rates than the National Minimum Wage and include specific junior percentages. Always check your award via the Fair Work Ombudsman's [pay guides](/blog) to see the correct rate for your job.

### Casual Loading

If you work casually, you are entitled to a **25% loading** on top of your base hourly rate. For an 18-year-old on the junior National Minimum Wage, the casual rate would be $18.51 × 1.25 = **$23.14 per hour**. The loading compensates for not receiving paid leave. When using our [the timesheet](/) calculator, you can check the 'casual loading' box to add 25% automatically—do not type a rate that already includes loading.

## Converting Hourly Pay to Annual, Fortnightly, and Weekly Figures

To convert your hourly rate to annual gross pay, use the formula:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, the calculation is straightforward. For part-time or irregular hours, use your average weekly hours.

### Example: 18-Year-Old on Junior Minimum Wage (Full-Time)

- Base hourly rate: $18.51
- Hours per week: 38
- Annual gross: $18.51 × 38 × 52 = **$36,575.76**
- Weekly gross: $18.51 × 38 = **$703.38**
- Fortnightly gross: $703.38 × 2 = **$1,406.76**

If you are casual, use the casual rate ($23.14):
- Annual gross: $23.14 × 38 × 52 = **$45,732.64**
- Weekly: $879.32, Fortnightly: $1,758.64

### When to Assume 38 Hours

We assume 38 hours per week for full-time work, as this is the standard under the National Employment Standards. If you work fewer or more hours, adjust the formula accordingly. Always use your actual weekly hours for an accurate estimate.

## Tax and Medicare Levy

Your annual gross pay is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office applies income tax and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the tax rates for residents are:

- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income between $18,201 and $45,000
- 30% on income between $45,001 and $135,000
- 37% on income between $135,001 and $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a **Medicare levy of 2%** (with possible reductions for low-income earners). For an 18-year-old earning $36,576 (junior minimum wage full-time), the tax would be approximately:
- Taxable income: $36,576
- Tax on first $18,200: $0
- Tax on next $18,376 ($36,576 - $18,200) at 15%: $2,756.40
- Medicare levy (2% of $36,576): $731.52
- Total tax and Medicare: **$3,487.92**
- Net annual take-home: **$33,087.84**

Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide for a more detailed breakdown, including the tax-free threshold.

## Superannuation (Super) Paid on Top

Your employer must pay **super guarantee** of **12%** of your ordinary earnings into a nominated super fund. This is on top of your gross pay—it is not deducted from your wages. For the junior minimum wage example:
- Annual super: $36,575.76 × 12% = **$4,389.09**
- Total employment cost to employer: $36,575.76 + $4,389.09 = **$40,964.85**

Super is capped at the maximum contribution base of **$270,830** per year, so it only applies to earnings up to that amount. For most 18-year-olds, this cap is not relevant. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Award Rates vs National Minimum Wage

Many 18-year-olds work in retail, hospitality, or fast food, which have specific awards. For example, the General Retail Industry Award 2020 sets junior rates at 70% for 18-year-olds of the adult level 1 rate (which is often higher than the National Minimum Wage). Similarly, the Hospitality Industry (General) Award 2020 has its own percentages. Always check your award using the [reference tables](/data) on our site to ensure you are paid correctly.

### Casual Loading Under Awards

Awards also include casual loading, usually 25% but sometimes different. The loading is applied to the base award rate, not the National Minimum Wage. For example, if your award rate is $22.00 per hour, the casual rate would be $27.50.

## Summary

- **Minimum wage australia 18 year old**: The adult National Minimum Wage is $26.44/hour; junior rate is typically 70% (~$18.51/hour).
- **Annual pay**: Hourly rate × hours per week × 52 (assume 38 hours for full-time).
- **Fortnightly pay**: Weekly pay × 2.
- **Casual loading**: Add 25% on top of base rate.
- **Super**: 12% paid on top of gross earnings.
- **Tax**: Use the 2026–27 resident tax scale and Medicare levy.

For a personalised calculation, use our [the timesheet](/) tool. Enter your base hourly rate (without casual loading) and check the casual box if applicable. The tool will show your annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures, plus estimated tax and super.

Remember, this is an estimate. Actual pay may vary due to unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. Always refer to your pay slip and consult the Fair Work Ombudsman if you have concerns about your wages.
